neighbours.label: ' it' as the subject of a clause embedded under 'as though/as if' or a feel/believe verb ('as though it were', 'feels it is')
fire: She held the old letter as though it were made of glass.
The farmer talked to his tractor as if it could understand him.
Many readers believe it is the finest novel of the decade.
He guarded the recipe as though it were a state secret.
The coach thinks it is too early to judge the new players.
They decorated the shed as if it were a palace.
Most of the staff felt it was unfair to cancel the trip.
The boy hugged the puppy as though it might vanish.
quiet: She held the old letter carefully and then put it in a drawer.
The farmer talked to his tractor while he fixed it in the yard.
Many readers bought it as soon as the novel came out.
He guarded the recipe and never wrote it down for anyone.
The coach watched it again on video after the match.
They decorated the shed and painted it bright blue.
Most of the staff liked the trip and wanted to repeat it.
The boy hugged the puppy and then carried it home.

notes: Card: ' it' 14 of the top 32, usually starting a counterfactual or belief complement; output suppresses reflexives. Probes: 'as though it were' 0.36, 'feels it is' 0.17, object 'bought it' 0.04, conditional main clause 0.03.
